title: Supplies - House of Pips Wiki
description: Every House of Pips supply: what it does, when to use it and where to get it.
html:
Supplies

Supplies are consumable items you keep in your Inventory between matches. Buy them in the Supply Shop with Bone Bucks, find them in Bone Boxes, or claim them on the Slap Track. Each one is used up when you spend it.

There are three kinds:

  • Table supplies are used during a match: on your turn, at the boneyard, or in the hand setup screen that opens before each hand.
  • XP boosts (Quick Study) and Bone Bucks boosts (Golden Ledger) are activated from the Inventory between matches and cover your next few matches.

Supplies are switched off in Old School, in Puzzles, and in any Custom match with the Old School modifier. Each supply has a limit on how many you can hold; the shop stops selling it once you reach the limit, and Bone Boxes refund extra copies as Bone Bucks. See Shop, Bone Boxes and cosmetics for the shop, Bone Boxes and the Slap Track.

Table Pass

Common Table supply

Skip one required boneyard draw and yield the turn. Usable only when you have no legal play.

In-game text · During a match

Use it on your turn when you have no legal play and the boneyard still has bones. Instead of drawing, you skip the draw and your turn passes to Rival.

  • It is only offered when a draw would otherwise be required.
  • It counts as a trip to the boneyard for perks: your play streaks reset and Lucky Pocket is ready for your next play.
  • Handy when the boneyard is full of bones you don't want, or when Leaky Pocket or Greedy Draw would make a draw expensive.
Where to get it90 Bone Bucks in the Supply Shop
Most you can hold3

Quick Study 1

Common XP boost

Earn 25% more XP throughout your next match.

In-game text · Activate between matches

Activate it from the Inventory between matches. Your next match earns 25% more XP from every source.

  • Activating another boost adds its matches to the queue instead of raising the bonus, so two Quick Study 1s cover two matches.
  • A queued boost is used by the next match you start in a mode that allows supplies. You can't activate a boost while a match is in progress or saved.
Where to get it90 Bone Bucks in the Supply Shop
Most you can hold3
Lasts1 match

Golden Ledger I

Common Bone Bucks boost

Earn 50% more Bone Bucks throughout your next match.

In-game text · Activate between matches

Activate it from the Inventory between matches. Your next match earns 50% more Bone Bucks.

  • Like Quick Study, extra activations add matches to the queue rather than raising the bonus.
Where to get it120 Bone Bucks in the Supply Shop

Blank Check

Epic Table supply

Change every blank half on one bone to a value from one to six. On 0-0, both halves change. The Epic pips determine placement and scoring.

In-game text · Before a blank play

On your turn, choose one of your bones with a blank and pick a number from 1 to 6: every blank half on that bone becomes that number. On the double blank both halves change, so 0-0 can become 6-6.

  • The bone keeps its new numbers for placement and scoring, and the game picks it up ready to play.
  • It needs a blank bone in your hand.
Where to get itNot sold in the shop: found in Bone Boxes and on the Slap Track
Most you can hold2

Boneyard Lantern

Common Table supply

For one trip to the boneyard, one fixed face-down bone is revealed.

In-game text · Before a hand

Use it in the hand setup screen before a hand. On your next trip to the boneyard, one random face-down bone is shown face-up before you choose.

  • If you don't visit the boneyard that hand, the light waits for your next visit in the same match.
  • The Boneyard Lantern perk does the same on every visit.
Where to get it135 Bone Bucks in the Supply Shop
Most you can hold3

Rail Pass

Rare Table supply

After an unplayable draw, inspect a second fixed bone and choose which one to keep.

In-game text · In the boneyard

When you draw a single bone that cannot be played and the boneyard still has another bone, the game offers to spend a Rail Pass. You then pick a second face-down bone, both are turned over, and you keep the one you want.

  • It is only offered on a plain one-bone draw.
  • If you decline, the draw finishes normally.
Where to get itNot sold in the shop: found in Bone Boxes and on the Slap Track
Most you can hold2

Pip Eraser

Rare Table supply

Reduce one open end by one for the next scoring calculation. The board itself does not change.

In-game text · Before a play

On your turn, choose an open end. On your next play, that end counts one pip less when the table adds up the open ends. The bone on the table doesn't change.

  • Use it to turn a total such as 16 into a scoring 15.
  • The erased end has to still be open after your play. If you play on that end it is covered, nothing is erased, and the Pip Eraser is still spent.

Worked example

The open ends are 6, 4 and 3. You erase the 6, then play 3-6 on the open 3. The ends are now 6, 4 and 6, which is 16, but the erased 6 counts as 5: the play scores 15.

Where to get itNot sold in the shop: found in Bone Boxes and on the Slap Track
Most you can hold2

Hammer Wax

Rare Table supply

If you win this hand and pass the hammer, your compensation draft has improved rarity odds.

In-game text · Before a hand

Use it in the hand setup screen. If you win that hand and pass the hammer to Rival, your compensation draft has better rarity odds: commons become much less likely and every higher rarity more likely.

  • It is spent when you use it. If you lose the hand, or win and keep the hammer, it is wasted.
  • See Matches, hands and drafts for the hammer and the compensation draft.
Where to get itNot sold in the shop: found in Bone Boxes and on the Slap Track
Most you can hold2

Dealer's Dare

Epic Table supply

Wager one eligible supply before a hand. Win to receive two copies; lose and it is gone.

In-game text · Before a hand

Use it in the hand setup screen and stake one of your supplies: a supply you own at least one of, that isn't at its holding limit, and isn't another Dealer's Dare.

  • Win the hand: you get two copies of the staked supply, up to its holding limit. That's one more than you staked.
  • Lose the hand: the staked copy is gone.
  • Dealer's Dare itself is used up either way.
Where to get it420 Bone Bucks in the Supply Shop
Most you can hold1
